the_finding: the alpha>=0.6 clause is unsatisfiable-by-construction on the r147 corpus: all 12 ground-truth labels are 'a1', so any judge set accurate enough to pass acc>=0.8 produces (near-)zero vote variance, and Krippendorff's alpha degenerates to ~0 regardless of agreement (the kappa-paradox; here d_o == d_e == 0.020833 with pooled counts a1:95 baseline:1 — the single non-a1 pick is a MIRROR leg, never a vote). The reliability the clause targets is established directly: 48/48 det votes unanimous, per-judge acc 1.0, answered 1.0, swap instability <= 0.083, miss-bias 0 on both arms.
the_decision: the strict pass=False stands on the record (never silently waived); the panel runs under pass_substance=True — the reliability evidence at its theoretical maximum; the owner/auditor adjudicates the clause's intent vs its artifact; the DIR-8 prefer-arm balance (6/6 a1-vs-baseline labels on future corpora) is the corpus fix that makes alpha computable
